item.title: Piyush Goyal signals scope for renewed China ties, says engagement must be fair and stable
item.description: India is open to business engagements with countries across the world, including China, provided the terms are fair and the geopolitical situation remains stable, Union Commerce and Industry Minister ...
item.content:encoded:
Piyush Goyal signals scope for renewed China ties, says engagement must be fair and stable India is open to business engagements with countries across the world, including China, provided the terms are fair and the geopolitical situation remains stable, Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said, signalling scope for renewed economic engagement with Beijing. ANI | Updated: 14-10-2026 10:29 IST | Created: 14-10-2026 10:29 IST

Union Minister Piyush Goyal (Photo/Youtube/Bloomberg New Economy). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

India is open to business engagements with countries across the world, including China, provided the terms are fair and the geopolitical situation remains stable, Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said, signalling scope for renewed economic engagement with Beijing. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, “We are open to all countries around the world as long as we get a fair deal, as long as we are ensured continuity in the engagement, and as long as the geopolitical situation does not deteriorate,” Goyal said during a panel discussion on supply-chain resilience and technology partnerships. “We are working to develop the relation with China once again, but the last word has not yet been scripted on this journey,” he added. Goyal also said India’s relationship with the United States remained strong and was expected to improve further, describing it as consequential for both countries and the wider world. He said the partnership extended beyond trade, with the US being India’s largest trading partner, to defence, technology, critical minerals and people-to-people ties. “I think the U.S. and India have a very, very consequential relationship, and it's only going to get better,” he said, adding that the ties were supported by economic, political and security imperatives and would remain strong despite changes in political thinking in either country. Goyal further highlighted that countries were increasingly seeking to develop their own technologies and equipment supply chains, making cooperation among trusted partners important. He said it might be difficult for individual countries to replicate capabilities concentrated in a few economies without working together. “It may not be possible that we can replicate what one or two countries have been able to do at really big scale unless we join hands, unless we work together,” he said. The minister said India was not pursuing isolation but wanted to balance self-sufficiency in critical sectors with efficiency through trusted international partnerships. He said countries needed to identify areas where dependence on external suppliers could make their production vulnerable to policy changes or geopolitical developments. Singapore Deputy Prime Minister and Trade and Industry Minister Gan Kim Yong said Singapore was working with India to strengthen the semiconductor industry and train workers to support its growth. He said cooperation remained important even as global economic and technology links faced fragmentation. During the panel discussion, Canadian Minister of International Trade Maninder Sidhu said Canada was accelerating efforts to diversify its trading partners and was negotiating a trade agreement with India. He said Canada’s energy resources could help meet India’s growing requirements, with India expected to need 70 per cent more energy by 2035. The discussion highlighted the growing emphasis on trusted partnerships, diversified supply chains and cooperation in technology and critical resources as countries respond to changing geopolitical and trade conditions. (ANI)

item.title: US Judge blocks Trump’s White House press ban on CNN, MS NOW, Politico, cites likely First Amendment violation
item.description: A US federal judge on Tuesday (local time) blocked President Donald Trump's attempt to bar journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, ruling that the administration's decision to ...
item.content:encoded:
US Judge blocks Trump’s White House press ban on CNN, MS NOW, Politico, cites likely First Amendment violation A US federal judge on Tuesday (local time) blocked President Donald Trump's attempt to bar journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, ruling that the administration's decision to revoke their press credentials likely violated their constitutional rights. ANI | Updated: 14-10-2026 09:54 IST | Created: 14-10-2026 09:54 IST

The White House (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

A US federal judge on Tuesday (local time) blocked President Donald Trump's attempt to bar journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, ruling that the administration's decision to revoke their press credentials likely violated their constitutional rights. US District Judge Timothy Kelly, who was appointed by Trump, granted a preliminary injunction, allowing reporters from the three news organisations to retain access to the White House grounds while their lawsuit against the administration proceeds. In a 26-page ruling, Kelly found that the revocation of the journalists' hard passes likely infringed their rights under the First and Fifth Amendments to the US Constitution. The decision reinforced the judge's earlier legal reasoning that the administration's action was likely retaliatory and violated constitutional protections for the press. Explaining his assessment of the president's decision, Kelly wrote that Trump's objections to the outlets' reporting appeared to have motivated the restrictions. “President Trump likely banned Plaintiffs from the White House because he believes that their reporting is generally inaccurate and biased against him,” Kelly wrote in the ruling. The judge also rejected the Justice Department's argument that national security concerns had at least partly prompted the decision to withdraw the journalists' credentials. "First, there is no evidence in the record that President Trump made the decision to revoke Plaintiffs’ hard passes on national security grounds from the get-go, nor at any time has he directly stated that national security was the reason for his decision," he wrote. The ruling follows a legal challenge brought by CNN, MS NOW and Politico after the Trump administration announced restrictions on their reporters' access to the White House. The news organisations argued that the decision was an act of retaliation over their coverage of the president and therefore violated the First Amendment's protections for freedom of speech and the press. The outlets also alleged that the administration violated their Fifth Amendment due process rights by revoking their press credentials without prior notice that their reporting could result in the loss of access or providing them an opportunity to respond before the decision was taken. Trump announced the restrictions last month, accusing the three organisations of engaging in what he described as "constant 'reporting' FAKE NEWS." The following day, journalists from the affected outlets who arrived at the White House were denied entry, while their press credentials were taken by the US Secret Service. CNN, MS NOW and Politico filed a lawsuit on September 21, challenging the administration's decision and arguing that their journalists had been singled out because of their reporting. The day after the lawsuit was filed, the White House Press Office sent letters to the organisations confirming the president's initial decision to revoke their journalists' credentials and giving them until September 25 to respond. The White House maintained that the journalists had failed to meet standards of professionalism and had published articles that raised national security concerns. However, Kelly's latest ruling rejected the administration's national security justification, noting the absence of evidence that such concerns had motivated the original decision to revoke the credentials. Trump had previously indicated that his administration would challenge an adverse ruling. In a post on Truth Social last month, he said the Justice Department would appeal if Kelly ruled against him. The preliminary injunction will remain in effect as the legal proceedings continue, allowing reporters from CNN, MS NOW and Politico to access the White House while the court considers the broader constitutional questions raised by the dispute. (ANI)

item.title: World leaders unite in prayers for Pope Leo XIV’s speedy recovery after successful lung surgery
item.description: World leaders on Tuesday (local time) have extended prayers and wishes for the speedy recovery of Pope Leo XIV following his successful lung surgery at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital, expressing hope for his ...
item.content:encoded:
World leaders unite in prayers for Pope Leo XIV’s speedy recovery after successful lung surgery World leaders on Tuesday (local time) have extended prayers and wishes for the speedy recovery of Pope Leo XIV following his successful lung surgery at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital, expressing hope for his return to health and highlighting his message of peace, humanity, unity and compassion amid his treatment for lung adenocarcinoma. ANI | Updated: 14-10-2026 09:52 IST | Created: 14-10-2026 09:52 IST

Pope Leo XIV (File photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

World leaders on Tuesday (local time) extended prayers and wishes for the speedy recovery of Pope Leo XIV following his successful lung surgery at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital, expressing hope for his return to health and highlighting his message of peace, humanity, unity and compassion amid his treatment for lung adenocarcinoma. The prayers come as the head of the Catholic Church recovers after doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung following a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio were among those who conveyed their prayers and wishes for the pontiff's recovery through posts on X. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described Pope Leo XIV as a source of inspiration for Catholics worldwide, emphasising his message of peace and humanity. "Pope Leo XIV is a source of inspiration to Catholics right around the world – and here in Australia. He is a voice for peace, humanity and reason in our modern world. My thoughts and prayers are with him as he recovers from his recent surgery. We hope and pray for a quick recovery," Albanese said in his post. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney also conveyed his wishes for the Pope's recovery, underlining the significance of his message of unity and compassion. "On behalf of Canadians, I wish Pope Leo XIV a full and swift recovery following his successful surgery. His Holiness is a source of hope and inspiration for billions around the world. His message of unity and compassion reminds us of the strength we can offer one another in moments of uncertainty. As he recovers, may he draw strength from the prayers of those whose lives he has touched, just as so many draw strength from him," Carney said. United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres also joined the global outpouring of prayers for the pontiff, wishing him a speedy recovery following his recent diagnosis. "Wishing His Holiness Pope Leo XIV a speedy recovery following his recent diagnosis. My prayers & thoughts are with @Pontifex & the Catholic community worldwide," Guterres said in his post. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed his prayers for the Pope's health, invoking divine guidance for the medical team overseeing his treatment. "Jeanette and I are united in prayer for @PONTIFEX’s health following his recent diagnosis. May the Lord give him strength and the Holy Spirit guide the medical professionals taking care of the Holy Father," Rubio said. The US Conference of Catholic Bishops also confirmed the successful removal of a cancerous tumour from the Pope's right lung, calling on the faithful to continue praying for his recovery and for those affected by cancer. "Doctors at Gemelli Hospital removed a cancerous tumor from Pope Leo XIV’s right lung, according to the Holy See Press Office. The surgery was successful, with no complications, and the Holy Father has returned to his hospital room. We ask the faithful to continue praying for Pope Leo’s recovery and for the doctors and staff caring for him. We also hold in prayer all who are living with cancer, their families, and those who care for them," the US Conference of Catholic Bishops said in a post on X. According to Vatican News, Pope Leo XIV underwent thoracic surgery at Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday afternoon, following preoperative examinations that confirmed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma. A statement from the Holy See Press Office said the procedure was carried out as planned, with doctors removing the lower lobe of the Pope's right lung using a video-assisted technique. “To ensure a radical resection, the lower lobe of his right lung was removed using a video-assisted technique. An intraoperative histological examination confirmed the diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, as suspected from the preoperative examinations,” the statement read. The Holy See Press Office confirmed that the operation was successful and that no complications occurred. The Pope spent approximately three hours in the operating room, with the surgery itself lasting around 90 minutes. “The operation was successful, and there were no complications,” the statement added. Vatican News reported that Pope Leo awoke normally after the procedure and returned to his room on the hospital's 10th floor following a brief period of observation. According to Matteo Bruni, Director of the Holy See Press Office, the Pope asked for dinner after the operation and spent the evening with his secretaries and other Vatican staff. The surgical team was led by Professor Stefano Margaritora, assisted by Professor Elisa Meacci, Dr Maria Teresa Congedo and Dr Leonardo Petracca Ciavarella. The anaesthesia team comprised Professor Massimo Antonelli, Dr Giovanni Punzo and Dr Giuseppe Bello. Further examinations of the removed tissue are expected to be conducted in the coming days, Vatican News reported. Preoperative tests had helped doctors determine the location of the affected tissue and the appropriate surgical approach. (ANI)

item.title: Duane “Keffe D” Davis sentenced to 40 years of life imprisonment for orchestrating murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur
item.description: Davis appeared in a Nevada court for his sentencing in the case, when the judge handed him 20 years to life for first-degree murder and 20 years to life for a deadly weapon enhancement.
item.content:encoded:
Duane “Keffe D” Davis sentenced to 40 years of life imprisonment for orchestrating murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur Davis appeared in a Nevada court for his sentencing in the case, when the judge handed him 20 years to life for first-degree murder and 20 years to life for a deadly weapon enhancement.  ANI | Updated: 14-10-2026 09:51 IST | Created: 14-10-2026 09:51 IST

Duane “Keffe D” Davis faces sentence for Tupac Shakur murder (File photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

30 years after the death of rap icon Tupac Shakur in 1996, Duane “Keffe D” Davis has been sentenced to 40 years to life in a Nevada prison for orchestrating the killing, reported Variety. On Tuesday, Davis appeared in a Nevada court for his sentencing in the case, when the judge handed him 20 years to life for first-degree murder and 20 years to life for a deadly weapon enhancement. Davis was facing a maximum of life in prison without parole. Prior to the judge’s decision, prosecutor Marc DiGiacomo pointed out a history of criminal activity and suggested that Davis “earned” the maximum sentence. “He’s an eight-time felon sitting before you on this crime perpetrated upon these family members, these family members, brothers. And you have to ask yourself, for this crime, for this person, what sentence does he deserve? Whatever your decision is, ultimately, in my mind, he deserves the maximum possible sentence because he’s earned it through his actions, his behaviour, and who he is as he stands here today,” he said, as quoted by Variety. Before handing down the sentence, Judge Carli Kierny went on to address Davis. “You don’t get to take a man from his family, you don’t get to take his very life, his whole future from him, and just walk away from it. Especially when that man is Tupac Shakur. The world never forgot about him and his death, and you are going to face justice,” Kierny said, as quoted by People. Davis’ defence attorney Michael Sanft further claimed that they would appeal the judge’s decision, while Davis addressed the judge, asking for his “stuff back” that was taken from his home. In court, the late rapper’s sister, Sekyiwa Shakur and brother Maurice Shakur urged the judge to sentence Davis to the maximum punishment. “Tupac is truly my shining star, my shining prince; he is who God trusted to take care of me. My mother had two children, and God gave him to me, and he’s supposed to be my life partner. I spent 30 years without my protection. I believe that if any life mattered, if all life matters, for sure this man’s life mattered. I do believe when you take a life like that, you deserve every minute, every minute, of the maximum amount of punishment, time to sit down and contemplate what you’ve done to this world. He had so much promise, intentions for a better world for our people; he had plans and manifestos. He’s so much more than street violence,” Sekyiwa said as she struggled holding back tears. In late August, Davis was found guilty of murder with use of a deadly weapon with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal gang. He was convicted after a weeks-long trial in Las Vegas, with prosecutors and police claiming that he orchestrated Shakur’s murder in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas on September 7, 1996. It was alleged that Davis handed the murder weapon to the gunman, believed to be either Davis’ nephew, Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson or another man in the car's back seat. Tupac Shakur was murdered in 1996 at a red light in Paradise, Nevada. He was shot four times, following which he succumbed to his injuries six days later. (ANI)
